Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private expansion: seamless cutover plan and term alignment

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier. Per Datasync's renewal, you mentioned adding two isolated production clusters (east/west) and a separate VPC for your analytics environment. To keep everything low-risk at cutover we propose the following high-level approach and commercial alignment: 

1) Operational cutover: blue/green environment fork with a staged canary (10%, 30%, 100%) and a 6-hour rollback window. We'll perform prefix/KV cache drain and a final KV snapshot prior to traffic shift. Estimated maintenance window: 4–6 hours on the chosen weekend.

2) Isolation & networking: dedicate a new VPC per environment with strict security groups and optional VPC peering to your telemetry collectors. KMS key mapping will be supported — we'll need the key ARN(s) and team contact for rotation coordination.

3) Capacity & term: provisioning request is for 3 additional GPU nodes per cluster (A100-equivalent), with a recommended 24-month committed term to secure the discounted pricing we discussed. With the commit, we'll include one free emergency burst day per quarter and a 10% unit discount on the incremental nodes.

4) Timeline & next steps: target cutover weekend is July 24–25. If that works, we'll send an updated SOW + DocuSign packet and a technical cutover checklist. Please confirm the window and whether SOC2 evidence and network diagrams need to be re-submitted for your procurement.

I've attached a draft cutover checklist and a pricing workbook so you can see the delta by region.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to walk through the plan.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private expansion: seamless cutover plan and term alignment

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few quick asks from our side before we lock the weekend: 

- Can you confirm whether the canary path will preserve existing session affinity for our inference clients (we rely on sticky sessions for some streaming use cases)?
- What is the expected RTO for KV cache warm-up after traffic moves? We need to know how long quality might diverge.
- Procurement asks for a one-page cost summary (incremental monthly commit) and a short SOW showing the timeline and acceptance criteria.
- We will need SOC2 Type II evidence and an updated network diagram to route to our security team.

If July 24–25 is the suggested cutover, we need your SOW and pricing summary by next Tuesday (July 6) to review legally and schedule procurement approvals.

Aisha
Head of Infrastructure, Datasync Health
a.bhat@datasync.io
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Private expansion: seamless cutover plan and term alignment

Marissa / Dev —

Aisha asked for specifics. Can you confirm the ops checklist items below and whether the July 24–25 window is viable from an infra capacity/support perspective? High-level items I want to cover in the SOW:

- Canary path details: 10% (pilot) -> 30% (expanded) -> 100% with 6h rollback window. Need to confirm sticky session behavior for streaming and whether we can do L7 routing to maintain affinity.
- KV cache plan: final snapshot, drain prefixes for 30min, warm-up strategy on green environment (est. 45–90min to reach steady-state for embeddings-heavy traffic).
- Network: new VPC per env, no cross-tenant peering by default, optional transit gateway for telemetry. Need firewall rule templates for their security team.
- KMS: support mapping, require ARNs and planned rotation window.
- Capacity: provisioning assumption is 3x GPU nodes per cluster (A100-class). Rough commit cost: $85,000/month incremental for the additional capacity (still draft until pricing workbook final).
- Commercial: 24-month committed term with quarterly emergency burst days included. Promo: 10% on incremental nodes.

Dev — can you validate the KV warm-up numbers and whether the runtime handles session stickiness via connection metadata? Marissa — can you confirm pricing band and whether CS needs to be standing by for the cutover?

I'll produce a 1-page cost summary & short SOW once you confirm these. I've attached the internal KV_Drain_Playbook for reference.

—Tessa
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Bhat <a.bhat@datasync.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Private expansion: seamless cutover plan and term alignment

Hi Aisha —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Confirming answers and next steps below (summary + attachments):

Answers to your questions:
- Sticky sessions: yes — the runtime supports L7 routing to preserve session affinity for streaming. We'll include the L7 routing template in the network diagram packet.
- KV cache RTO: conservative estimate 45–90 minutes to reach steady-state for embeddings-heavy traffic; we will perform a pre-cutover warm-up using replayed low-volume traffic to reduce divergence.

What you'll get by July 6 (per your procurement request):
- One-page cost summary (attached: Datasync_Augmented_Fleet_Pricing.xlsx) showing incremental monthly commit and per-token economics.
- Short SOW (attached inside DocuSign packet) with timeline, acceptance criteria (canary success thresholds, data-integrity checks, rollback triggers).
- SOC2 Type II evidence link and updated network diagram (SOC2 link included in DocuSign packet).

Operational notes: we recommend the July 24–25 weekend. If approved, we'll schedule a technical kickoff with infra + security teams the week of July 12 to walk the cutover checklist. Please review the attached cutover checklist and let me know any required additions.

Next actions for you: confirm the cutover weekend and the signatory for the DocuSign packet; if you confirm both, I'll send the SOW and DocuSign link today so procurement can start their review.
